content.thinking:
I'm planning out the whole roadside shrine scene in one pass: a torii gate, stone lanterns, a small hokora shrine, stone path, fox statues, shimenawa rope with shide and tassels, a bell, offerings like fruit and sake bottles, plus surrounding plants and a maple tree, all built carefully using the geometry/part API without testing as I go.

For structure, I'll create one root joint for the shrine base and a separate hinge joint for the bell so it can sway, keeping everything else as plain parts. I'm leaning toward an Inazuma-inspired color palette — vermilion lacquer red, cream stone, gold filigree, purple accents, and electro-glow lanterns — using cel shading for large surfaces and flat colors for smaller details.

Now I'm sketching the overall layout: a torii gate at the front with a stone pathway leading back to a hokora shrine, flanked by stone lanterns and simple stylized kitsune statues, with an offerings table of sake barrels, bowls, and candles in front of the shrine.

I also need small decorative elements like a maple tree, bamboo cluster, grass cards, sakura petals, and shide paper zigzags, plus ema plaques -- these will need their own SVG textures. Now I'm working out the ground base as a low-poly octagonal slab sized to hold the whole scene symmetrically along the x-axis.

Setting ground height at 0.12 so everything sits on top without sinking, and planning pathway stones as boxes placed at that height. For the box helper function, I'm making sure every part explicitly attaches to the root bone rather than whatever joint happens to be nearest, since parts near the bell could otherwise mistakenly bind to the bell joint instead of staying rigid.

Now I'm sketching out the shrine (hokora) layout, placing it at z=-1.2 with a bell hanging from a porch beam over the offering box, and defining the stone platform as a wide, shallow box sitting just above ground level.

Still working out shrine proportions: the lifted wooden floor, red lacquer walls, lattice doors, and a hip roof built from a lathe shape with four segments.

Working out the lathe spin orientation for the roof, figuring that with 4 segments and a 45° spin the faces should align to the axes, giving a half-width of radius times cos45 — so a 0.95 target half-width needs roughly r=1.34. Still defining the profile points for the roof shape.

I'm finalizing the roof outline points and picking a deep purple-toned color scheme with gold ridge accents for an Inazuma-style roof, plus thinking through how to add tile stripe details and a gold finial on top via custom paint logic.

Now I'm figuring out the hip ridge rods -- gold cylindrical rods running diagonally from the eave corners up toward the roof's peak point.

Deciding to skip the full front porch structure and just hang the bell from a simple bracket under the front eave, with a short horizontal beam near the roofline supported by two small posts.

Working out the z-coordinates so the roof eave, posts, bell, and saisen offering box don't overlap -- I'm shifting the saisen box toward the front ground area instead of the platform to avoid clashing with the bell rope and posts.

Still working out positions: posts at z=-0.55 spanning the platform height, a kasagi crossbeam at y 1.22, and the bell hanging at the same z. For the saisen box I'm checking it doesn't collide with the bell rope's drop point, so I'm nudging the rope/bell to z=-0.62 to clear it.

Now I'm planning the three stone steps leading to the platform, sizing each box progressively narrower, and laying out a stone path from z=-0.1 to 3.0 with slight random yaw per slab. I'm also setting up the torii gate at z=1.6 with tapered pillars at x=±1.05.

Writing torii lintel sweep...

Now I'm adding the tie beam that extends slightly beyond the pillars, plus a central gaku plaque between beams with a geometric rune instead of text, red-painted pillars with gold bands and a black skirt ring at the base, and a sagging shimenawa rope with shide hanging between the pillars.

Now I'm detailing the shide zigzag paper texture and hanging tassels along the rope, then building a reusable stone lantern function with hex-lathed base, bulging pillar, flared platform, a glowing firebox core, and a curved roof topped with a jewel finial.

Writing lathe geometry for lantern parts...

Still shaping the lantern geometry...

Adding the jewel finial profile, I total the stack to about 1.35m tall, suitable for a garden tōrō mounted at ground level. I'll wrap everything in a lantern function taking position, scale, and base height, with a helper that scales and offsets every point consistently.

Since lathe geometry doesn't support a scale option directly, I'll build both lanterns at identical size for simplicity, maybe adding smaller hanging chōchin lanterns on the posts instead for variety. I'm writing a small helper function to scale outline point arrays by a factor before passing them into the lathe geometry.

Now I'm laying out the shrine scene: torii pillars, flanking kitsune fox statues on pedestals, and paper lanterns positioned along the path, working out specific x/z coordinates for each element and sketching the fox body shape as a curved sweep from rump to chest.

Still placing fox geometry...

Adjusting tail radius taper and settling on round caps for the sweep. Since the two foxes are mirrored and symmetric, I just need a single fox function parameterized by x and z position. For the bib, I'll use a thin flattened torus ring around the neck for the cloth detail.

Adding a gold bell sphere at the chest and an extruded diamond shape for the hanging bib cloth, positioned slightly overlapping the chest. Now I'm thinking through the offering altar setup on the platform, placing a sake barrel beside the saisen box as one of the offerings.

I'm designing a pair of straw-wrapped rice barrels using lathe geometry with rope hoops and wooden lids, positioned symmetrically on the platform. For the offerings I'm also adding a kagami mochi stack with a mikan on top sitting on a small sanbo stand, plus fruit offerings like apple spheres.

I'm adding sake bottles with painted labels near a small wooden table, an incense burner, and an ema rack with hanging wooden plaques featuring painted designs—built as extruded wood shapes rather than textures, held up by two posts, a crossbar, and a small roof. I'm also placing a maple tree at the back left with a swept trunk and canopy.

I'm scattering falling cherry petal cards, adding a cel-shaded icosahedron-cluster sakura tree with curved branches, a bamboo clump with jointed stalks and leaf cards, mossy flattened-icosahedron rocks, grass tufts, and shide paper streamers on the shrine's shimenawa rope and torii gate. I'm considering adding small glowing elemental crystal orbs above the stone lanterns as a Genshin-style touch.

Now I'm adding a glowing violet glyph decal on the top step, floating purple petals and orbs near the shrine, and a glowing gem on the shrine door, while keeping total part count under budget. I need to make sure every card and prop references a bone -- setting up a root joint plus a bell joint for the bell parts, and planning hinge joints for the shrine doors so they can swing open.

Setting up door hinges and panels...

I'm placing the door box at the front wall depth and positioning the lattice plane just in front of it so the pattern overlays the door surface. I want the texture to include a dark wood background fill plus gold lattice lines rather than transparent cutouts, so the door's red paint doesn't show through unintentionally.

Now I'm sketching the SVG designs: a crimson door panel with gold lattice lines and a golden seal medallion centered on it, matching each door half.

For the ema plaques, I'm planning four variants with wood fill and red borders using simple icon motifs (star, moon, leaf, flower), cut into a pentagon shape with alpha transparency so they hang as card-like plaques facing forward along the frame's flow direction.

I need to account for how hanging cards appear from the viewing side: since the flow axis points toward the viewer, the drawing on the card actually appears upside down with the root edge on top, so to make the ema look correctly oriented I'll need to flip my SVG drawing 180 degrees before applying it to the card.

Rather than fight with the orientation math, I'll simplify by extruding a wooden plaque shape with thickness, then layering a front-facing plane with the SVG decal on top (transparent outside the drawn shape), with the plaques mounted on the rack facing the viewer.

For the shide paper strips on the shimenawa, I'll draw a zigzag fold pattern that reads reasonably whether flipped or not, so orientation quirks don't matter much. For scattered petals lying flat on the ground, I'll use a pink petal SVG with alpha cutout, randomizing rotation and flow direction for natural variation.

Grass gets two-tone cel-shaded blade clumps scattered manually around the perimeter avoiding the path, with varied sizes and random lean. For tree foliage, I'm using icosahedron canopy blobs flat-shaded pink with cel style, plus a few ring-shaped blobs for variety, and scattering fallen petal cards along the stone path.

Now I'm setting up the color palette inspired by Genshin's Inazuma aesthetic -- lacquer red with purple-shifted shadows, gold tones using cel shading for larger pieces, and mottled stone textures for lantern surfaces with automatic shadow resolution.

I'm layering moss onto the stone using a noise-based paint function that applies green where the surface slopes upward and a noise threshold is crossed, then defining wood grain textures, dark wood accents, and a purple-striped roof color scheme with glow accents in purple and amber.

For the ground, I'm setting up a mottled grass-and-dirt pattern on a cylinder, painting grass on the top face and earth tones on the sides based on surface normal direction. I also need to keep an eye on the total count of distinct flat colors used across parts, staying under the 64 limit by relying on shared palette constants.

Now I'm sorting out the type definitions — settling on a `Fill = string | Paint` type so colors and paint patterns can be passed interchangeably to builder functions like `rod` and `sweep`. Then I start writing the actual build function, creating the builder instance and placing a root joint for the shrine at the origin.

Setting up the geometry helpers next...

Now planning the scene pieces starting with the ground plane as a faceted low-poly cylinder, then roughing out the layout for the path, rocks, and torii gate placement.

Checking placements for the shrine, tree, and bamboo so they stay within the ground radius, and scattering mossy icosahedron boulders around the rim for edge detail. Then moving to the stone path slabs laid out in a sequence across the ground.

Now I'm adding a pale gravel bed beneath the path slabs, flanking them on either side with a long low box textured in cream tones, which will frame the path composition nicely spanning the ground.

Next I'm designing the platform and staircase: a stone platform base with a thinner trim layer and coping edge on top, then building three descending steps of decreasing width leading up to it, positioning each step's height and depth along the z-axis in front of the platform.

Still working out step heights and widths, then moving to the shrine body: four corner posts as red cylinders positioned symmetrically at the platform edges.

Now I'm adding the walls and sub-floor foundation, using a lighter cream plaster color between the posts, and starting to place the front doors at the entrance.

Adding small lattice windows on the side walls with a faint warm glow, then planning railing posts with gilded finial balls at the platform corners connected by thin rail rods.

Still placing porch posts and crossbeam...

Then I'm planning a gold finial sphere at the roof peak with an onion-shaped lathe top, and writing a custom paint function for the roof's color gradient along its height.

Now I'm adding gold eave decorations—small spheres placed at each corner of the roof's edge.

I'm also planning hanging fuurin bells at the corners with gold castings and paper tassels, plus a shimenawa rope with shide hanging between the front posts, sagging slightly below the crossbeam.

Actually, I realize the rope path might collide with the suzu bell, so I'm moving the shimenawa to wrap around the sacred tree trunk instead, leaving the shrine's bell free at center front near the base of the gate.

Still placing the bell geometry...

I'm placing the rope hanging from the bell down to the front edge where people stand, keeping it near the platform's front z-position, and positioning the saisen offering box dimensions near the base.

For the top of the box, I'm adding thin dark grill rods across the opening, gold trim boxes front and back for the frame, and scattering a few tiny gold coin discs on top as offerings.

Now I'm positioning sake barrels on either side of the shrine, adjusting their placement so they don't collide with the railing posts, and working out the barrel dimensions with straw-colored hoops using a scaled profile and torus shapes.

I'm adding a wooden lid at the top and a small label plate on the front face of each barrel, abstracting a sake label design with a red circle and gold bars since specific fonts aren't available.

Now I'm placing the kagami mochi stack and considering where to put an offering table, deciding to skip crowding the box and instead reposition the lanterns and fox pedestals along the path at wider spacing to avoid overlap.

I'm checking lantern placement against the torii pillars and slab positions to make sure everything fits within the ground circle radius, then adding a small offerings table to the left side with legs and a tabletop at a safe distance from the path edge.

Thinking through the offering details: kagami mochi stacked discs with a shide strip, sake tokkuri bottles with sakazuki cups, apples in a woven bowl, onigiri with nori strips, and dango skewers with pink, white, and green spheres. I'm positioning this offerings table around x=-1.65 to keep clear of the fox statue and lantern nearby.

For the right side, I'm placing an ema votive rack with two posts, a crossbar, and a small gabled roof made from a lathe-pyramid shape, plus bamboo and rocks clustered nearby for balance. I'm working out string-like rods to hang the plaques from the crossbar at the right height.

I'm figuring out two rows of plaques (four each) hung from separate crossbars, with each plaque built from a small extruded pentagon shape plus a hanging plane and knotted string -- around 40 parts total, with slight random yaw rotation for a natural look.

Defining pentagon coordinates...

Still drawing fox face... I'll also sketch the moon crescent, sakura petals, and purple lightning bolt variants, wrapping them in a shared helper function. Hanging strings get a red color.

Now I'm designing the torii gate structure—black lacquer kasagi top, red lacquer pillars tapering with radius arrays, and black cylindrical bases—thinking through whether pillars should lean slightly inward like a real torii.

I'm adding gold fittings at the nuki beam ends and pillar tops, plus a dark wood plaque between the pillars bearing a simple abstract crest, avoiding anything resembling a real logo.

Checking overall torii dimensions against the tree to make sure proportions work, then I'm sketching the shimenawa rope as a curved sweep across the front.

Still writing shimenawa details...

I'm also adding chochin paper lanterns hanging from the nuki beam near the ends, glowing amber-red with black caps and strings, while double-checking the vertical placement so the shimenawa rope hangs correctly below the nuki rather than overlapping it.

Let me try hanging the lanterns from the kasagi instead, further out at x=±1.5 so they clear the pillars by a good margin, checking that the string length and chochin position stay below the kasagi's curved underside without colliding with the nuki ends.

For the tree, I'm placing it back-left at (-2.0,-1.6) clear of the shrine platform, building the trunk as a tapering catmull-rom sweep with shrinking radius toward the top, then adding rod-like branches and icosahedron canopy blobs in pink. I need to keep the canopy top under roughly 3.1 so the tree doesn't exceed the torii's overall height.

Lowering the canopy centers slightly to keep the top near y=3.05, then scattering small petal cards across the blob surfaces using a two-tone pink texture for added detail and softness.

For the shimenawa rope, I'm figuring out how to wrap a closed loop around the trunk at height 1.1, matching the trunk's radius there and offsetting slightly outward so the sweep sits cleanly on the surface without needing exact axis alignment.

For placing the shide paper cards along that loop, I'll avoid the `along` helper's uncertain callback signature and instead just sample points directly via the loop path's `.at(t)` method, which is simpler and guaranteed not to fail.

Now I'm designing the bamboo stalks — five rods clustered off to one side with striped node rings created via a y-based paint pattern, then scattering small leaf cards near the top of each stalk with varied lean and flow angles.

Beyond that, I'm placing mossy flat-shaded boulders near the shrine corners, finalizing the stone lanterns at fixed positions, and deciding to skip extra small lanterns to keep the scene from getting cluttered.

I'm adding a handful of glowing purple orbs and gold octahedra floating above the shrine as decorative motifs, plus a glowing circular sigil decal laid flat on the ground path in front of the shrine.

I'm laying out slab positions along the z-axis, leaving the .0–.95 range clear so the sigil can sit as a paved ritual circle on the gravel instead of overlapping the slabs.

Now I'm checking placement conflicts between foxes, lanterns, and the step - adjusting fox pedestal position and step width so they don't collide, then positioning lanterns at x ±1.05 to clear the fox bases.

With positions settled, I'm making glowing elements use flat colors for the cel-shaded look, then generating grass card decorations on the ground - sampling random positions on the disc while excluding the path and platform regions, targeting around 140 accepted cards.

Now I'm adding small flower cards scattered around (roughly 30), plus fallen petal cards along the path, working out the layering so petals sit at the right height whether they're over gravel or slabs without floating or clipping.

I'm also tallying up the full object budget: ground, gravel, rocks, slabs, platform, steps, and the shrine itself with its posts, beams, doors, windows, roof details, wind chimes, and gold fittings, to make sure everything stays within scope.

Finishing the broader scene inventory next -- torii gate, lanterns, foxes, offering table, ema rack, tree, bamboo, and orbs -- landing around 420 triangles total, which feels reasonable. Now I'm setting up the code imports for the builder and type definitions before writing the actual construction logic.

Setting up the shrine builder with root joint, randomness seed, and an outline-point helper for scaling coordinate arrays.

Still defining box helper options...

I'm importing the PartOptions type to simplify the signature, then sketching helper shortcuts for cylinders, spheres, and toruses with sensible default geometry and rotation. I'm also planning a lathe helper that wraps profile points with spin and bone options.

Now I'm defining the rod helper using SweepOptions for building swept geometry between two points, then starting a plane helper for flat rectangular surfaces with textures and directional placement.

I'm thinking through how direction vectors map to orientation axes for the plane—working out fallback perpendicular logic when the up vector is parallel to the aim axis, so decals lying flat still orient correctly. Then I'm considering how color/texture paints share a single sheet, noting that texel density drops as the total painted area grows, since resolution scales with the square root of coverage.

I'm estimating the shrine's total painted area at roughly 60 square meters, giving a texel density around 9mm, and deciding to bump the paint size to 2048 for crisper cel-shaded edges without pushing the atlas too heavy. I'm also sketching out the color palette, defining lacquer reds, gold tones, and a stone base color, with a seeded stone function for variation.

Defining more material shaders...

Still defining materials, then I'm sketching the grass, gravel, and torii colors before moving into the lantern geometry function, starting with its base shape coordinates.

Writing lathe coordinates for the lantern pillar and ring...

Still placing lantern bars and roof segments...

Still building the fox statue geometry...

Adding inner ear detail and darker pink coloring, then placing the eyes as small dark slit-shaped boxes angled slightly for a slanted fox-eye look.

Now I'm building out the legs and paws with rod and box shapes, sizing the hind thigh spheres, and sketching the tail as a curved sweep through a series of points.

Still shaping the fox details...

Now I'm moving to the offerings table setup near the shrine, planning a wood tabletop with four legs and apron, plus a cloth runner with gold trim draped over it.

Adding kagami mochi stand...

Adding the fruit bowl with apples, then setting up a dango stand with a skewer holding pink and white dango spheres angled in a small cup.

I'm also adding a triangular onigiri with a dark nori strip and a small candle with an amber glowing flame near the table. Checking that the torii pillars and ema rack positions don't collide with the table or lanterns.

Writing SVG grass blades...

Still writing petal and leaf SVG shapes...

I'm redefining the shide zigzag path with cleaner left/right edge points to avoid self-intersection, then adding a fold line stroke, before moving on to designing the lattice door SVG at 60x80.

For the door, I'm sketching a maroon background with a gold border and a diagonal lattice pattern, considering using a defined SVG pattern or a loop to generate repeated diagonal lines efficiently rather than hardcoding each one.

Designing door clipping with diamond lattice lines, a gold border, and center medallions with purple gems, then moving to the side window's warm glow lattice and the gaku emblem with a lightning-style central motif.

Still writing SVG assets...

Designing the chochin lantern shape with a lathe profile for the paper body, flat orange-red glow color, dark red rib tori spaced around it, plus black caps top and bottom and a tassel strand.

Adding wind chime details...

Checking that the roof base radial dimensions clear the walls, with overhang sized generously for the stylized look. I'm placing a support beam under the roof, positioning gold corner brackets angling from wall tops to the eave corners, and adding window planes on the side walls aligned with the wall faces.

I'm skipping window frame details in favor of the SVG border, adding a small gold emblem plane on the back wall, and leaving the roof ridge bands and ground rope sigil out for simplicity. For the rocks scattered around the rim, I'm generating them with randomized scale and rotation using icosahedron geometry and moss coloring, distributing them angularly around the perimeter while skipping placements near the front path opening.

Now I'm building the torii gate detail, constructing the black base platforms, tapered pillars, gold rings and collars near the crossbeam, and gold end caps on the nuki beam for each side of the gate.

Adding the chochin lanterns and shaping the kasagi crossbeam as a tapered frustum, then working out the red shimaki sweep path with proper box-section radii aligned to the local path orientation...

For the gaku plaque, I'm layering a tie-rod column behind a dark rectangular plaque box, positioning them both centered above the torii crossbeam.

I'm checking spacing so the plaque doesn't collide with the nuki beam, so I'm nudging its y position up a bit to avoid overlap while keeping the plaque's front and back planes properly sized to match its SVG aspect ratio.

For the shimenawa rope, I'm verifying its attachment points align with the nuki's bottom edge so the ends touch naturally while it sags in the center, without conflicting with the plaque's position.

Writing rope paint pattern...

Then I'm placing shide (paper streamers) along the rope at several fractional positions, sizing them small and tinting them white to suggest the paper cards hanging from the sacred rope.

Now I'm figuring out barrel placement for offerings on the platform, checking the x and z coordinates against the saisen box and railing posts to make sure the barrels don't overlap the posts, settling on roughly ±0.82 for the x position.

Building the barrel's lathed profile and rope/label geometry...

Now I'm checking the shrine joints and skeletal structure—placing the root joint and attaching the bell joint via a hinge relationship, then working out the door attachments.

Now I'm building the tree trunk as a tapered sweep along a curved path with bark texture, then adding flaring root rods at the base.

Adjusting blob heights so the canopy doesn't get too tall, then defining the blossom color with a mottled pink shadow tone, and scattering petal cards onto the blob surfaces based on normal direction.

Now I'm positioning a shimenawa rope loop near the trunk's axis and setting up a sweep to render the rope geometry.

I'm laying out bamboo stalks with varied positions and heights, building each as a tapered rod from base to tip.

For coloring, I'm painting node stripes along the bamboo with alternating green shades and applying cel shading for a consistent lit look. Then I'm scattering leaves near the top of each stalk with slight lean and tinted coloring, before moving on to place rocks near the bamboo base.

Now I'm building the ground disc as a flattened cylinder, adding a stone border ring, and placing grass cards while excluding areas near paths, platforms, and tree trunks using polar-distributed random positions.

Next I'm adding flower cards in smaller counts with similar frame logic, then scattering fallen petals across gravel, slab, and ground zones with randomized orientation and slight height offsets to sit just above each surface.

For orbs, I'm using glowing purple spheres with increased strength, octahedron gold shapes for stars with scaled geometry, and skipping extra halo rings or sigil effects around lanterns and pedestals to keep the scene from getting too busy.

Now I'm setting up the fox pedestals and importing the toon ink color for eye details, plus pulling in the builder, frame, path, paint, and texture utilities needed for the final scene assembly. Writing imports...

Still writing fox code...

Checking that joint ordering and bone assignment don't matter here, and deciding to move all paint definitions inside the build function so repeated builds stay consistent rather than relying on module-level caching. Now defining the roof paint function with a banding pattern based on position.

Switching to a derived shadow variant for the roof's cel shading so ridge lines stay visible in shadowed areas, then moving on to composing the rest of the structure -- ridge sweeps, stone lantern pillars, and the lathe profile points for the roof geometry.

Now I'm adding the gold ridge corner details using a catmull-spline sweep, a lathe-built onion finial at the roof peak with a small decorative ring, and gold sphere caps at the eaves corners.

Writing ema rack code...

Still placing roof and plaques...

Skipping the tassel detail for now. The ema rack position, offering table, torii stones, and toro tops are set, so I'm turning to decorative gold touches -- considering small gold end caps at the kasagi tips and a filigree band trim along the platform front to match the shrine's ornate style.

Writing SVG swirl pattern...

Writing the diamond lattice SVG generator...

Finishing up the window colors and diamond styling, then double-checking the card flow function types and table leg coordinates before finalizing the full file.
